answer: Sybil farms win when one operator mints many short-lived keys and grabs seats. This intake requires each claimant to plant a stake on the east knoll, publish a 32-byte kernel commitment bound to that stake nonce, then run a 1.8 km tundra transect whose GPS mid-point sits within 3 m of the stake. Cost is a 31.2 POA bond plus a 14-hour cooling hold, too slow for one window. Peers recompute the kernel from the published preimage and match the track to the stake photo hash. A reused stake, a colliding kernel, or a mid-point miss slashes the bond and bars the seat until two closes pass.
